newsitem.title: THAILAND: TelecomAsia sees no impact from baht float.
newsitem.headline: TelecomAsia sees no impact from baht float.

text.p: Thai telecommunication firm TelecomAsia Plc said on Wednesday the central bank's move to adopt the floating foreign exchange system will have no impact on the company's cash flow as most foreign loans are long term.
"Most of the liabilities we have in foreign currencies were in the long term and to be due for payment in about 10 years," TelecomAsia said in a filing to the Stock Exchange of Thailand.

The Bank of Thailand announced earlier that it intended a "managed float" of the Thai baht and said the value of the baht would be set by market forces instead of being pegged to a basket of currencies.
Analysts said the central bank's move to float the baht was a de facto devaluation.
TelecomAsia did not give its total outstanding foreign loans, but analysts said the company's foreign loans are about 60 percent of its total liabilities of 86 billion baht ($3.07 billion).
At midday, TelecomAsia's shares had gained three baht to 34.25. ($1 = 28 baht)
